_comment: EDGE-1 PROBE (docs/HANDOFF_edge_response_queue.md edge 1): is the closed-loop /
replay consumer's SSR datum-break reaction path actually INERT, as SPEC
SS25.5 / SS27 item 2 assert, or merely SILENT?
Finding that motivated this arm: runConsumerReplay drives a RealTimeEngine, and
RealTimeEngine::processEpoch calls all five RealTimeEngineSsrBreaks handlers
UNCONDITIONALLY (RealTimeEngine.cpp:479-483) — including resetOnPhaseBiasDisc,
which resets an ambiguity on every producer phase-bias discontinuity-counter
step.  The counters are recomputed deterministically on replay
(NetworkProductReader::replay -> emitter.emitToStore), and the emitter's phase
jump test is UNGATED at kDefaultDiscThresholdM = 0.05 m — below every one of the
387 mid-arc steps > 0.1 m the SS25.2 census found.  So the reactions should be
firing.  The reason runs/replay_ext63_12h_ref/logs/rt_engine.log is EMPTY is that
logging.enable_rt_engine defaults to FALSE (GnssConfigLoad.cpp:3075), so every
reaction line was suppressed.
This arm is byte-identical in SOLVE to _ext63_replay_12h_ref.json — the ONLY
delta is logging.enable_rt_engine, which writes a log file and changes no state.
Grade: count 'SSR phase-bias discontinuity: reset' / 'code-bias discontinuity' /
'clock discontinuity' / 'generation-id changed' lines in rt_engine.log, and
confirm closed_loop_trace.csv reproduces the reference arm exactly.
Extends _ext63_gps_dual_1h.json DIRECTLY and restates every override of
_ext63_replay_12h_ref.json (SPEC SS23.7 extends-chain depth ceiling is 8; the
reference replay config already sits at 8, so this is a SIBLING, not a child).
